parsed.explanation: The worst documented features are tier-1: border adjudication that refuses cases where sex is in reasonable doubt and can convert a marker/presentation mismatch into a permanent fraud ineligibility, feeding into immigration custody where trans detainees are documented as beaten, held in solitary and sexually abused; and a division that has stripped gender identity from its civil-rights statute and preempted local remedies, leaving the outed visitor no recourse for service refusal. Facilities exposure is real but narrower for adults — the division's birth-certificate restroom rule binds everyone on school grounds but no general-public adult restroom statute is documented. No criminalisation of trans identity, no death penalty, functioning courts and a national hate-crime statute keep this above the 0.25 anchors; the absence of any working remedy and the severity of custody harm keep it below the 0.35 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Screening cable directs refusal where documents or records cast reasonable doubt on sex, with possible permanent lifetime ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation; X markers unprocessable; trans athletes barred; governments issued advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic; litigation ongoing and some orders enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Visa/entry adjudication → secondary inspection → refusal or fraud referral → possible immigration detention; discrepancy can migrate across stages.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections model imposes hair-cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution on trans inmates; prison LGBTQ order rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts have enjoined several executive orders; no documented custody protocol protecting trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy can become a fraud allegation, then detention, then birth-sex placement with documented harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division 2025 law fixes binary sex at birth; 2023 school rule requires birth-certificate-matching restrooms/changing rooms on school grounds, binding all present including visitors and guardians; national facility bans widespread.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-person alternative written as a student accommodation conditional on guardian consent; no adult general-public restroom statute documented in this division.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor attending a school event falls under the birth-certificate rule; outside school grounds exposure is undocumented rather than absent.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care under 18; national measures pressure providers, insurers and records; subpoenas of hospital patient data.
care_services.protection: Division high court preserved adult surgery coverage (resident-facing); one city bans conversion therapy for minors; national insurance rule is proposed and contested.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian cannot obtain care here; adult visitors' records requests can expose identity.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for rapid neutralisation; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; executive order targets teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo states powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises discovery consequences and police suspicion without documented arrests of trans visitors on this basis.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban under 18 in the division; school-facility rule reaches accompanying guardians; national order contemplates prosecuting those who affirm a minor's transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented for travelling minors; adoption and parentage protections are resident-facing only.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian accompanying a trans minor on school grounds is exposed by the same rule; care needs go unmet locally.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific violence data; national counts described as undercount floors; legal-risk grades predict state behaviour, not private conduct.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; division bias-statute coverage not established; no division civil-rights remedy since repeal.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting an assault yields a federal channel at best; the division route for gender-identity bias is removed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender identity removed from division civil-rights law from 1 July 2025; 2026 preemption of stronger local ordinances; refusals of service are unremedied at division level.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal hate-crime statute; ongoing litigation; legal-aid guidance on document rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse depends on federal forums and courts rather than the division that would handle a hotel, venue or police complaint.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar document-mismatch secondary screening and denial of entry, but 0.35-A has a statute barring detention for mismatch. Here detention is not barred and immigration custody is documented as abusive, and ineligibility can be permanent — materially worse.

0.25-B has coercive custody, coerced statements and extortion under vague public-order statutes; this dossier shows no street-level extortion or arbitrary arrest, but shows state-imposed border refusal and severe documented custody harm plus no civil-rights remedy — comparable severity, higher institutional formality, so a little above.

0.55-B features a working supervisor intervention and a lawful remedy (guidelines applied, permit issued). No working remedy for the trans visitor is documented here; the division has removed its own protections, so this sits clearly below.

0.45-D involves a visible registry flag, service denial and slow mediation, with no criminal or custody exposure. Here the exposure chain reaches entry refusal and abusive detention, and local mediation is unavailable — worse than 0.45-D.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a chain rather than a set of isolated rules: a marker or presentation mismatch at the border can trigger refusal, a misrepresentation referral carrying lifetime ineligibility, and detention in a system where trans detainees are documented as abused. Inside the division the traveller finds gender identity stripped from civil-rights law and local remedies preempted, so a refusal of lodging or service has no route to redress; the only recourse is federal, and federal posture is itself hostile though partly enjoined. Facilities exposure is genuine but narrower for adults — the birth-certificate restroom rule binds visitors on school grounds, and no general-public adult restroom statute is documented. Absent criminalisation or capital exposure, this sits in the high-risk band but not at its floor.
